results.diagnosis: pandas 3 infers a nullable string dtype, so astype(str) preserves missing labels instead of rendering them as "None"/"nan" for value_counts to retain, and DataFrame.value_counts(sort=False) no longer returns the lexicographically group-sorted order of pandas 2. Forcing object dtype, stringifying labels elementwise with Python str, and explicitly sorting the count index restores the pandas 2 semantics on both versions, while retaining DataFrame construction so ragged/empty rows are filled and then dropped by value_counts as missing.

pandas 3 preserves missing values through astype(str) using the new string dtype (so None/''-derived NaN rows are dropped by value_counts) and DataFrame.value_counts(sort=False) now returns first-appearance rather than sorted-index order; the fix forces object dtype and Python str() conversion to preserve 'None'/'nan' strings, and explicitly sorts the counts by (team, label).

pandas 3 infers a string dtype that preserves missing values through astype(str), so value_counts(dropna=True) drops None/empty-derived labels, and DataFrame.value_counts(sort=False) now returns appearance order instead of the old groupby-sorted order.
